item.title: Mike Ogilvy 美国行
item.description:
Mike Ogilvy 美国行

PVG 🛫 SFO

Berkeley and UC berkeley

传 送 点

乘坐BART到达Downtown Berkeley，这就是我在美国的传送点。美国的BART和杭州地铁又有些不同，总的来说有三点不同：

1. 手机信号极差 2. 站间距离长 3. 班次没那么密集

总体来说，更像轻轨而不是地铁，感觉想要真正体验美国的地铁，还得飞到新乡去。

Town / City

如果对应到中国的行政区划，伯克利和西湖区平级，属阿拉米達縣，如果对应城市规模，那大概和三墩镇差不多。这是一个很安静的小镇，几乎没有高楼，不过给人一种“一应俱全"的感觉，具体来说就是有公交车有超市有奶茶店（特指Heytea，因为Heytea可以买一送一，适合偶尔想消费的时候喝），可以满足我的生活需求。

UC Berkeley

走进伯克利-大学，仿佛走进一个真正的“大学”。这么说的原因当然是因为对于本科生来说，某个东方Caltech毫无大学的感觉，而是更像一个研究所。（并没有诋毁母校的意思）校园里植被遍布，生机盎然，其中分布最广的是松树🌲，在伯克利，只要有一块没有被硬化的地面，那么你一定可以看到松鼠从一棵松树跳到另一棵。

伯克利整个校园是依山而建的，在有坡度的土地上的建筑总有一个明显的特征，那就是——没有一个准确的1楼。以李嘉诚先生捐赠修建的Li-Cai-Shing Center为例，你可以从其中一个门进入，走楼梯往上一楼，再从另一个门出来，颇有一种“盗梦空间”的感觉。

San Francisco

The Golden Gate Bridge 金 门 大 桥

人民教育出版社的编委们把这座多灾多难的桥作为封面，Apple公司把她的剪影做成emoji🌉，可以见得这座桥在旧金山甚至美国的重要性。更重要的是，党和国家领导人习近平主席曾经到访旧金山，并曾在桥前留下影像记录。正因为这样的重要性，我选择在落地的第一个周末就前往金门大桥。

可能是因为雾蒙蒙的天气，实地看来桥的红色并没有那么鲜艳，不过这并不能阻挡我用蹩脚的后期技术把她修的艳丽一些。海面很蓝，蓝的有些深邃，海面上看起来很“拥堵”，游艇，摩托艇，帆船“川流不息”。桥的旁边是大片的草地和沙滩，孩子和狗在浅滩上疯跑，着实让我羡慕。

在桥的一侧眺望，可以看到恶魔岛

San Francisco Downtown 市 区

旧金山市区和伯克利有很大区别，有一种真正的“大城市”的感觉。China Town和银行街连在一起，有一种建筑突然升高的空间压缩感觉。建筑非常密集，即使是在盛夏，街道上依然见不到很多阳光，反而有一股淡淡的凉意。

旧金山的China Town颇有中西融合的味道，在这里你能看到三种旗帜交相呼应，分别是美国国旗，中国国旗和中华民国国旗，从公交车下车就能看到中國國民黨駐美國總支部，也算是一种奇观了。

在China Town的本地华人也几乎没人说普通话，不如改叫 Guangdong Town。

San Jose

Tech Company

虽然贵为首府，San Jose没有我刻板印象中高楼耸立的大城市的感觉。乘坐有轨电车穿梭在市区里（人生第一次乘坐有轨电车🚋），感觉整个城市冷冷清清（也有可能是周末的原因）。

item.title: Making RTX 4060 Passthrough Work on an AMD Laptop
item.description:
GPU passthrough is usually presented as a short checklist: enable IOMMU, bind the GPU to vfio-pci, add a PCI host device, and boot the guest. That model breaks down on laptops, where firmware controls GPU enumeration and also supplies the ACPI tables that describe IOMMU isolation.

On my ASUS ROG Zephyrus G14 GA403UV, the RTX 4060 was in a clean IOMMU group and was correctly bound to VFIO, yet QEMU still refused to start the VM. The useful part of the exercise was not the final XML. It was isolating the failure to an incorrect IVRS table and fixing only the affected PCI bus.

item.title: GEARS Explained: How Graph Neural Networks Predict the Unseen
item.description:
A deep dive into the model that can forecast what happens when you knock out genes nobody has ever touched.

The Problem

You’re a biologist. You have a Perturb-seq dataset — 100,000 cells, each with one or two genes CRISPR-knocked out, plus single-cell RNA-seq readouts of the full transcriptome. You’ve experimentally perturbed 100 single genes and 130 two-gene combos. But there are 4,950 untested pairwise combinations. Running them all would cost a fortune.

item.title: ML-2 Note: Linear Models for Classification and GLMs
item.description:
1. Why Classification Uses Logistic Regression

In classification problems, the target variable is discrete.

Binary classification example:

$$y \in \left\{ 0,1 \right\}$$

Given input features

$$x \in \mathbb{R}^d$$

we want to model

$$P(y=1|x)$$

Problem with Linear Regression

A linear model predicts

$$f(x) = w^T x$$

but

$$w^T x \in (-\infty, \infty)$$

while probabilities must satisfy

$$P(y=1|x) \in [0,1]$$

Thus we need a function that maps

$$(-\infty,\infty) \rightarrow (0,1)$$

Logistic Function

The logistic (sigmoid) function provides this mapping

item.title: ML-1 Note: Supervised Learning; Linear Regression
item.description:
1. Basic Model of Linear Regression

Linear Regression is one of the simplest and most fundamental models in supervised learning.
The goal is to model the relationship between input features and a continuous target variable.

Model Form

For a dataset with feature vector \(x\):

\[ y = w^T x + b \]

or equivalently

\[ \hat{y} = \theta^T x \]

where:

  • \(x\): input feature vector
  • \(w\): weight vector
  • \(b\): bias term
  • \(\theta\): parameter vector (including bias)
  • \(\hat{y}\): predicted value

Loss Function

The most common loss function for linear regression is Mean Squared Error (MSE).

item.title: Learning and Practice of Single-Cell Sequencing
item.description:
Abstract

Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has become an essential technique for studying cellular heterogeneity and complex biological systems. During this winter research training, I systematically studied the general workflow and analytical principles of scRNA-seq based on Single Cell Best Practices and related resources, covering key steps such as data preprocessing, quality control, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and cell type annotation. To consolidate the knowledge, I first reproduced a complete analysis pipeline using publicly available immune cell data to familiarize myself with standard procedures and tools, then independently applied the same workflow to a publicly available human brain infection-related single-cell dataset, identifying distinct cell populations and infection-associated transcriptional changes across cell types. Overall, this training deepened my understanding of scRNA-seq data analysis, demonstrated the adaptability of standardized workflows to diverse biological contexts, and provided preliminary insights into cellular responses in infected human brain tissue as a foundation for further studies.
